ccel.title: ANF03. Latin Christianity: Its Founder, Tertullian

source.title: ANF03. Latin Christianity: Its Founder, Tertullian
ANF03. Latin Christianity: Its Founder, Tertullian

verses.text: But we more commend our prayers to God when we pray with modesty and humility, with not even our hands too loftily elevated, but elevated temperately and becomingly; and not even our countenance over-boldly uplifted.
verses.modernizedText: But we more commend our prayers to God when we pray with modesty and humility, without raising even our hands too high, but raising them moderately and fittingly; and not even our face lifted too boldly.

verses.text: For that publican who prayed with humility and dejection not merely in his supplication, but in his countenance too, went his way “more justified” than the shameless Pharisee.
verses.modernizedText: For that tax collector who prayed with humility and dejection not merely in his supplication, but in his face too, went his way “more justified” than the shameless Pharisee.

verses.text: The sounds of our voice, likewise, should be subdued; else, if we are to be heard for our noise, how large windpipes should we need!
verses.modernizedText: The sounds of our voice, likewise, should be subdued; otherwise, if we are to be heard because of our noise, how large a windpipe would we need!

verses.text: But God is the hearer not of the voice, but of the heart, just as He is its inspector.
verses.modernizedText: But God is the hearer not of the voice, but of the heart, just as He is its inspector.

verses.text: The demon of the Pythian oracle says:
verses.modernizedText: The demon of the Pythian oracle says:

verses.text: “And I do understand the mute, and plainly hear the speechless one.”
verses.modernizedText: “And I do understand the mute, and plainly hear the speechless one.”

verses.text: Do the ears of God wait for sound?
verses.modernizedText: Do the ears of God wait for sound?

verses.text: How, then, could Jonah’s prayer find way out unto heaven from the depth of the whale’s belly, through the entrails of so huge a beast; from the very abysses, through so huge a mass of sea?
verses.modernizedText: How, then, could Jonah’s prayer find its way out to heaven from the depth of the whale’s belly, through the entrails of so huge a beast; from the very abysses, through so huge a mass of sea?

verses.text: What superior advantage will they who pray too loudly gain, except that they annoy their neighbours?
verses.modernizedText: What superior advantage will those who pray too loudly gain, except that they annoy their neighbours?

verses.text: Nay, by making their petitions audible, what less error do they commit than if they were to pray in public?
verses.modernizedText: Nay, by making their petitions audible, what less error do they commit than if they were to pray in public?
